semantic_binding.rep_eq_sumConv: rep A n = sum over antidiagonal n of 1_A p.1 * 1_A p.2 -- the object studied IS the upstream sumRep; ORDERED pairs, diagonal counted once
semantic_binding.Erdos28Stmt: the upstream erdos_28 restated with sumRep replaced by the bound rep
semantic_binding.convention_warning: the ORDERED convention is what makes the floor 2 rather than 1; an unordered reading shifts every statement here by a factor of two

reformulation.limsup_eq_top_iff: limsup (rep A n : ENat) = top  <->  r_A is NOT bounded by any B, uniformly on all of N
reformulation.erdos28_iff_no_bounded_basis: Erdos 28  <->  no set is simultaneously an additive basis of order 2 and a B2[B] set
reformulation.erdos28_iff_every_bound_exceeded: Erdos 28  <->  for every basis A and every B there is an n with rep A n > B. This is the exact gap: the campaign proves B = 1 is exceeded and nothing more.

FLOOR.swap_mem_rep_set: the swap (a,b) -> (b,a) preserves the representation set of n
FLOOR.two_le_rep_of_odd: n odd and rep A n >= 1  =>  rep A n >= 2 (the swap has no fixed point at odd n)
FLOOR.one_le_rep_of_basis: (A+A)^c finite  =>  there is M with rep A n >= 1 for every n > M
FLOOR.two_le_rep_odd_of_basis: hence rep A n >= 2 for every large ODD n
FLOOR.frequently_two_le_rep: hence rep A n >= 2 frequently along atTop
FLOOR.two_le_limsup_of_basis: THE FLOOR: limsup (rep A n : ENat) >= 2 for every additive basis of order 2
FLOOR.not_rep_le_one_of_basis: equivalently, no additive basis of order 2 has rep A n <= 1 for all large n
FLOOR.two_le_bound_of_basis: any uniform bound B on rep A for a basis satisfies 2 <= B

SANDWICH.sum_rep_eq: sum_{n<=N} rep A n = #{ordered pairs from A of sum <= N}
SANDWICH.sum_rep_le: sum_{n<=N} rep A n <= cnt A N ^ 2
SANDWICH.le_sum_rep: cnt A (N/2) ^ 2 <= sum_{n<=N} rep A n
SANDWICH.basis_count: (A+A)^c finite  =>  there is M with N - M <= cnt A N ^ 2 for every N
SANDWICH.cnt_sq_le_of_rep_le: rep A <= B everywhere  =>  cnt A N ^ 2 <= B * (2N+1) for every N
SANDWICH.counterexample_sandwich: a counterexample has 2 <= B and N - M <= cnt A N ^2 <= B(2N+1)
SANDWICH.counterexample_sandwich_real: explicitly sqrt(N - M) <= |A cap [0,N]| <= sqrt(B(2N+1)): the counting function of any counterexample is Theta(sqrt N)
SANDWICH.counterexample_structure: THE STRUCTURE THEOREM: everything the campaign knows about a counterexample, in one object
SANDWICH.erdos28_iff_no_theta_sqrt_basis: the Theta(sqrt N) clause is FREE -- adding it to the target costs no generality

KILLS.parity_saturates_at_two: ROUTE KILL. The function n |-> (2 if n odd else 1) is positive everywhere and even at every odd n -- every constraint the parity route places on r_A -- while never exceeding 2. Hence NO argument from those constraints alone can prove limsup r_A >= 3.
KILLS.parity_and_moment_saturate_at_two: ROUTE KILL, EXTENDED. The same function additionally satisfies sum_{n<N} f(n)^2 <= 4N, so positivity + parity + ANY linear second-moment bound is jointly consistent with r_A <= 2.
KILLS.not_parityAdmissible_implies_three: the negative form: 'every parity-admissible function exceeds 2 somewhere' is FALSE
KILLS.why_the_moment_axis: Ruzsa 1990 constructs a REAL additive basis of order 2 with sum_{n<=N} r_A(n)^2 = O(N), so the second moment cannot separate bounded from unbounded r_A. CITED, not formalised here.

SUMMARY.campaign_state: floor 2, route dead at 2, target = 'every bound B is exceeded' -- one object
SUMMARY.what_remains: the target restated as the non-existence of the structure the campaign pinned

independent_finite_verification.window_search_data: min_max_rep = 2 for N in [2,5], 3 for N in [6,12], 4 for N in [13,16]
independent_finite_verification.window_search_ceiling: EXTRAPOLATION REFUSED. A window-covering set is NOT an additive basis of order 2 -- the two conditions are neither a subset nor a superset of one another -- and a minimum over a finite window transports to nothing infinite. This is boundary-audit data, never a trend.

honest_comparison: The published record is >= 8. This campaign proves >= 2. The banked value is the machine-checked formalisation, the counterexample structure theorem, and the two route kills -- NOT a new bound. Nothing here approaches, let alone closes, Erdos 28.

PRIOR_ART_DEPTH -- the >= 6 and >= 8 records and the Ruzsa construction are at STATEMENT_MATCHES from search snippets only; none was read in its published form, and the ordered/unordered convention of sigma_A is UNVERIFIED.

RECORD_GAP -- formalising Borwein-Choi-Chu (>= 8) would lift the floor from 2 to 8 with no new mathematics. It was NOT attempted: the proof is a substantial finite computation over the structure of initial segments and is out of budget for this campaign.

THIRD_AXIS -- the kills cover positivity, parity, and linear second moments. They say NOTHING about routes using higher moments, the analytic Erdos-Fuchs machinery, or the structure of A itself. Naming the next axis and killing or opening it is the highest-value next attack.
